capabilities: Log workout sessions with one tap from weekly routine slots
Track weekly sets per body part against routine volume targets
Record powerlifting lift weights with PR and progress charts
Show sessions, streaks, totals and a month activity calendar
Embed activity calendar and quick-log widgets in notes
extras: Works on desktop and mobile with no internet connection required. Exercise library and rehab content are seeded into the vault as user-owned markdown notes with an explicit disclaimer that Rehab is not a substitute for a clinician. Widgets are in-note code blocks, not home screen widgets, because Obsidian mobile has no plugin widget API; home screen launching works via a registered URL scheme through Apple Shortcuts or Android shortcuts.
motivation: The author optimizes for showing up rather than logging detail, and wants training history to stay as plain markdown that remains readable and queryable even if the plugin disappears.
problem: Workout apps keep training history in their own silos, and Obsidian has no built-in way to log sessions as queryable markdown.

relations.evidence: Flat frontmatter, so Dataview and Bases can query your training history without the plugin.
Flat frontmatter, so Dataview and Bases can query your training history without the plugin.

summary: Opinionated, mobile-first workout tracker that logs sessions as sets per muscle group and stores each session as a plain markdown note in the vault.
